title: Fine-Tuning LLMs Without Retraining Everything

sections.heading: Everyday Analogy
sections.body: Think of a big language model like a trained chef who knows every recipe. Fine-tuning is like teaching that chef your family's special dishes. You don't send the chef back to school for years. You give a small recipe book with examples. LoRA means low-rank adaptation, a tiny add-on that changes just a little. Quantization means shrinking the model to use less memory, like compressing photos.

sections.heading: Why It Exists
sections.body: Why do we need this? Full training costs too much and needs huge computers. PEFT means parameter-efficient fine-tuning, a way to train only the small add-on, not the whole chef. You format your dataset into prompt and answer templates, so the model learns the pattern. SFTTrainer is a Hugging Face tool that handles this training loop for you. Then you can run it locally with Ollama, so it works on your own computer.

sections.heading: What Can Go Wrong
sections.body: What can go wrong? Bad dataset formatting teaches the wrong pattern, like typos in recipes. If you shrink too much with quantization, quality drops. If your LoRA add-on is too small, it won't learn; too big and it overfits, meaning it memorizes your examples but fails on new ones. Local deployment can also fail if your computer lacks memory.

steps.narration: Start with a pre-trained large language model, your big chef.
Shrink it with quantization so it fits on your GPU.
Format your examples into clear prompt and answer templates.
Use SFTTrainer to train only the small LoRA adapter, not the whole model.
Attach the adapter and run it locally with Ollama.

quiz.q: What does LoRA do in fine-tuning?
options: Retrains every weight in the huge model
Adds a tiny trainable add-on while freezing the base model
Deletes the base model to save space
quiz.why: LoRA is a PEFT method that trains a small low-rank adapter instead of all parameters.

quiz.q: What fails first if you fine-tune on 20 poorly formatted examples and deploy locally?
options: The model will perfectly generalize to any question
Dataset formatting errors cause wrong patterns and overfitting, plus local memory may run out
Quantization will automatically fix the dataset
Ollama will make the model larger
quiz.why: Bad templates teach wrong patterns, tiny data leads to overfitting, and shrinking/deployment has memory limits.

quiz.q: What is quantization with bitsandbytes for?
options: To shrink the model to use less memory/GPU
quiz.why: Quantization compresses model weights so a large model can load and fine-tune on smaller hardware.

judge.why: D1 starts with an everyday chef analogy, defines LoRA, quantization, PEFT, SFTTrainer and Ollama in plain beginner words within the length limit, and its quiz tests real understanding. D2 mislabels forgetting as overfitting, while D3 is clear but longer and denser than the target.
